sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Alonso rules Caicedo and Palestra out of the Leeds cup tie; Colwill is fit
briefs.summary: Xabi Alonso said Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra are "still not ready to go, and it's not the moment to take an early risk" for Wednesday's Carabao Cup third-round tie with Leeds at Stamford Bridge, 3 p.m. ET (8 p.m. BST); Emmanuel Emegha and Jordan Henderson also stay out, and Levi Colwill is available after sitting unused at Arsenal. "No matter the context, games between Chelsea and Leeds always matter," Alonso said.

briefs.headline: Iraola calls his first Champions League night at Anfield 'special'
briefs.summary: Andoni Iraola takes Liverpool into the Champions League league phase against Diego Simeone's Atletico Madrid at Anfield Wednesday at 3 p.m. ET (8 p.m. BST), saying he feels "privileged to be there in that dugout" and that Simeone's teams are "starting to have more possession of the ball." The club says Bradley Barcola is "ready to play more minutes"; Chiesa, Bradley, Ekitike and Leoni are out. Simeone said Julian Alvarez is available only from the bench.

briefs.headline: Skubal and the Dodgers beat the Reds 3-2; Lowder faces Yamamoto tonight
briefs.summary: Tarik Skubal held Cincinnati to four hits over 7 1/3 innings Tuesday at Dodger Stadium and Tanner Scott got his 22nd save; Elly De La Cruz's 25th homer, a two-run shot in the third, was the Reds' only scoring. Will Smith homered and Teoscar Hernandez went 3-for-3 for Los Angeles, which scored single runs in the first, second and fifth off Nick Lodolo. The Reds are 69-76, fifth in the NL Central. Rhett Lowder faces Yoshinobu Yamamoto Wednesday at 10:10 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Pirates beat the White Sox 9-3 behind Chandler and 18 hits
briefs.summary: Pittsburgh scored five in the first and two in the second off Sean Burke, who got four outs and allowed eight hits and seven runs, Tuesday at Rate Field; Bubba Chandler went six innings on four hits with no walks and eight strikeouts. Rafael Flores had three hits and a homer and Spencer Horwitz drove in three. The Pirates are 72-73, third in the NL Central and 5.5 out of a wild card. Lake Bachar faces Davis Martin Wednesday at 7:40 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Browns' first depth chart has Judkins, Boston and Fano starting
briefs.summary: Cleveland's unofficial Week 1 depth chart, released Tuesday, lists Deshaun Watson at quarterback, Quinshon Judkins at running back, Jerry Jeudy and Denzel Boston at receiver and rookie Spencer Fano at left tackle with Tytus Howard on the right. The Browns also signed receiver Bub Means and defensive end Nadame Tucker to the practice squad. Kickoff at Jacksonville is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez says WVU 'played it too close to the vest' after halftime
briefs.summary: West Virginia had 24 points and 336 yards in the first half against Coastal Carolina and seven points and 77 yards in the second, throwing five passes after the break; Rich Rodriguez said "we probably played it too close to the vest in the second half with the lead" and "I could have been more aggressive, especially in the third quarter." Tennessee-Martin visits Saturday at 1 p.m. ET on ESPN+.

briefs.headline: Gibson says Marshall will not let Penn State 'derail our season'
briefs.summary: Tony Gibson said the shutout loss at Penn State was "very disappointing," that the Herd "weren't very good on third down on either side of the ball" and "missed a lot of tackles," but that film showed Kelvon McBride "played really, really well." "Everything we want is still in front of us. We're not going to let one game against Penn State derail our season," he said. Middle Tennessee visits Saturday at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN+.

briefs.headline: Hauser points to Jacksonville State's quarterback and a 6-foot-8 receiver
briefs.summary: At his Monday press conference John Hauser said Jacksonville State quarterback Caden Creel "can run, he can throw" and "makes the thing go," and that 6-foot-8 receiver DeAndre Johnson is the matchup problem; he wants Ohio to run more after "light boxes" went unused at Nebraska, where the line allowed "zero sacks." The Gamecocks visit Peden Stadium Saturday at 6 p.m. ET on ESPN+.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Kirishima wins 19 of 21 at the joint practice four days before the basho
briefs.summary: Ozeki (champion) Kirishima, seeking promotion to yokozuna (grand champion), won 19 of 21 bouts Wednesday at the Tokitsukaze group's joint practice at Ryogoku Kokugikan, beating new sekiwake Fujinokawa seven times in eight bouts. "I have no nervousness at all," he said. Yokozuna Hoshoryu, who practiced Tuesday without a knee brace, had no practice report by Wednesday evening and says he will decide on the basho (tournament) by Friday. It opens Sunday at Kokugikan.

briefs.headline: Onosato wins 11 of 20 against Hiradoumi as Aonishiki sweeps 15 bouts
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato won 11 of 20 straight bouts against maegashira Hiradoumi at Sakaigawa stable in Tokyo on Wednesday; he said the first three or four "were poor," and stablemaster Nishonoseki said he was "receiving too much." Ozeki (champion) Aonishiki, a day after resuming bouts on his left ankle, won all 15 against a sandanme (third-division) wrestler at Ajigawa stable and will not face top-division opponents before Sunday's opening. "I have no anxiety," he said.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat the Cubs 4-3 in 10 innings for a second straight night
briefs.summary: Jackson Chourio's two-run homer in the ninth tied it and Luis Lara's bases-loaded single in the 10th won it Tuesday in Milwaukee, a night after a 4-3 win over the same Cubs; Chourio went 4-for-5 and DL Hall was the winning pitcher and Caleb Thielbar took the loss. The Brewers, 90-56, lead Chicago by nine in the NL Central. The Rays beat the Braves 7-1 and the Astros beat the Phillies 6-5, leaving Atlanta's NL East lead at four; the Yankees beat the Rockies 5-3 and trail Tampa Bay by four.

briefs.headline: Guardians beat the Orioles 9-5 on Bazzana's three-run homer
briefs.summary: Travis Bazzana's three-run homer, his 11th, capped a four-run second inning in Baltimore on Tuesday and Cleveland led 6-0 after three; Pete Alonso's 34th homer, a two-run shot in the fifth, was as close as the Orioles came. Tim Herrin got the win and Brandon Young fell to 9-4. The Guardians are 74-72, two games behind the White Sox in the AL Central.

briefs.headline: NFL opens tonight in Seattle with Henderson out for the Patriots
briefs.summary: The Patriots play the Seahawks at 8:20 p.m. ET Wednesday on NBC. The final injury reports rule out New England running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and center Ben Brown (knee) and Seattle safety Ty Okada (hamstring); safety Nick Emmanwori (ankle) and receiver Tory Horton (hamstring) are questionable for Seattle, and Mike Macdonald said Emmanwori "looks great." The 49ers and Rams play Thursday at 8:35 p.m. ET in Melbourne.

briefs.headline: Villa beat Club Brugge 3-2 and City beat Porto 2-0 to open the Champions League
briefs.summary: Aston Villa scored three times in 43 minutes through John McGinn, Emiliano Buendia and Nicolas Jackson, then held on Tuesday in Bruges after Hugo Vetlesen and a Nicolo Tresoldi penalty. Erling Haaland scored in the 47th and 91st minutes at Porto to equal Sergio Aguero's Manchester City record of 36 Champions League goals in Enzo Maresca's first European match as City coach. Real Madrid beat Inter 2-1 on goals by Federico Valverde and Kylian Mbappe.

briefs.headline: Shelton beats Alcaraz in five sets in the latest finish in U.S. Open history
briefs.summary: Ben Shelton came through five sets against Carlos Alcaraz, closing it out 10-7 in a final-set tiebreak at 3:33 a.m. ET Wednesday after 4 hours, 28 minutes, the latest finish on record at the tournament; the ATP says it was his first win over a top-three opponent after 17 losses. Alcaraz had 53 unforced errors to Shelton's 34. Shelton next plays Frances Tiafoe, who came from two sets down against Alex Michelsen.

briefs.headline: Sabalenka beats Noskova in two tiebreaks for a sixth straight U.S. Open semifinal
briefs.summary: Top seed Aryna Sabalenka came through three sets against Linda Noskova on Tuesday, taking the first and third in tiebreaks in 2 hours, 22 minutes after trailing 4-2 in the decider, extending her run at Flushing Meadows to 18 matches and keeping a bid for a third straight title alive. Noskova hit 46 winners and 18 aces to Sabalenka's 42 and 12. Sabalenka next plays Jessica Pegula, who came from a set down against Emma Navarro.

briefs.headline: LSU rises to No. 8 and Michigan drops out of the AP Top 25
briefs.summary: Monday's AP poll moved LSU up to No. 8 after its rout of Clemson in Lane Kiffin's first game and dropped Michigan from No. 16 to unranked after its last-second win over Western Michigan, the only ranked team to fall out; Virginia entered at No. 25. Oregon fell from No. 2 to No. 6 after a narrow win over Boise State. Ohio State, Georgia, Notre Dame, Texas and Indiana are the top five; the SEC won all 16 of its Week 1 games, the first time since 1997.

sections.note: Sumo copy was read on Yahoo Japan article pages carrying Kyodo, Sponichi, Nikkan Sports and Sports Hochi reports from Wednesday afternoon in Tokyo; the JSA's English site listed no withdrawals Wednesday and says tickets are sold out for all 15 days. Hoshoryu's decision on entering comes by Friday's bout-drawing meeting, and no Wednesday practice report on him had surfaced by 6 p.m. Tokyo time. Fujinokawa, the first sekiwake (junior champion) from Kyoto in 198 years per Hochi, went 7-12 at the joint practice. Takayasu, 36, told Hochi on Tuesday he will compete despite a strained thigh. r/Sumo could not be swept: the fetch tool refuses old.reddit.com. The Aki basho opens Sunday, Sept. 13, at Ryogoku Kokugikan, four days out, and runs through Sept. 27. The NFL Kickoff game is Wednesday, Sept. 9, not Thursday as this paper's ledger had it; the 49ers and Rams play Thursday at 8:35 p.m. ET in Melbourne. Wednesday's Champions League slate in ET: Barcelona-Feyenoord and Stuttgart-Viking at 12:45 p.m.; Liverpool-Atletico Madrid, Napoli-Arsenal, PSG-Slovan Bratislava and Sporting-Galatasaray at 3 p.m. The Patriots' reported four-year, $135 million extension for cornerback Christian Gonzalez, carried on the club site as per NFL Network, had not been announced by the team. Frances Tiafoe meets Shelton and Jessica Pegula meets Sabalenka in the semifinals.

prime.item: Limits page effective Sept. 2: an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day, harvest reported to the division; the Fisherman's Post September report, published Sept. 1, has Native Son on a steady dock-and-creek-mouth bite starting on topwater early, and Speckled Specialist finding reds scattered in small groups around bits of structure.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, with one fish over 25 inches allowed; the Sept. 1 Fisherman's Post report has Surf City Pier's bottom fishing holding up with black drum, pompano and croakers, and Coastal Angler has them at the bridges, docks and oyster rocks on cut shrimp.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 12-inch fork-length minimum and 15 per day; the Sept. 1 report has Jolly Roger Pier calling the Spanish and bluefish hit-or-miss for anglers sight-casting plugs, Spring Tide finding size and numbers varying by the hour, and South End Adventures getting bigger fish over hard bottom in 45 to 50 feet.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 14-inch total-length minimum and five per day, no federal rule; neither September report names them, so this is the seasonal pattern, not a live report: fiddler crabs tight to pilings and oyster rock on moving water, which today means the fall into the 1:31 p.m. sound low.

going_out.item: Day nine of the two-week window, which closes at 11:59 p.m. Monday, Sept. 14, under proclamation FF-27-2026, read again this morning: one fish per day, 15-inch minimum, one daily limit per person aboard a vessel, no harvest under a Recreational Commercial Gear License, and the harvest must be reported. Carolina Flats' Sept. 1 report has a strong class of 20-to-24-inch fish inshore with the mullet thick.

The early Canada goose season closes Sunday, Sept. 13, four days out, per the DNR's 2026-27 migratory bird summary: five a day and 15 in possession, in aggregate, with HIP registration required. The regular goose season does not open until Oct. 3.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

sections.note: The DNR's 2026-27 migratory bird summary opened again Wednesday with readable text: youth waterfowl Sept. 19 and Oct. 31, early Canada geese Sept. 1-13, mourning dove Sept. 1-Oct. 11, Nov. 2-15 and Dec. 7-Jan. 10 at 15 a day, rails Sept. 1-Nov. 9, snipe Sept. 1-Dec. 16, ducks Oct. 3-11, Nov. 7-15 and Dec. 21-Jan. 31, woodcock Oct. 17-Nov. 21 and Nov. 30-Dec. 8, and no September teal season in West Virginia. North Carolina's September teal season is not printed with a date: the only Wildlife Resources Commission table that opened is headed 2025-26, and it is that agency's season, not Marine Fisheries'. Marine Fisheries' proclamation index shows nothing issued Sept. 7-9 and the limits page is still the one effective Sept. 2; the bluefish table says 5 a day but the footnote caps private anglers at 3. Gauley season opens Friday, Sept. 11: the National Park Service whitewater page, updated Aug. 26, lists Corps releases from Summersville Dam on Sept. 11-14, 18-21 and 25-28 and Oct. 2-5, 9-12 and 17-18, and Gauley Fest runs Sept. 17-20 at Nicholas County Veterans Memorial Park in Summersville per American Whitewater. The Forest Service on Tuesday closed two sections of Forest Road 76, the Cranberry River Road, in the Gauley Ranger District through Nov. 20 for construction. The first Chief Logan elk tour is Sunday, Sept. 13, per the DNR's Aug. 28 release as carried by Lootpress; the wvdnr.gov page carrying Sept. 6 is last year's. WVDNR's National Hunting and Fishing Day is Saturday, Sept. 19, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. at Stonewall Resort, adults $10 and 14 and younger free; the national observance is Sept. 26. The DNR's stocking page lists no waters stocked. NWS Charleston says the city's 10.92 inches in August was its wettest August on record.

waters.working: Down from 101 cfs at this hour yesterday and back to low, clear late-summer water. At 55 cfs this is a long-leader, small-fly river: a 12-foot leader to 6X, a size 16 or 18 caddis or a small stonefly nymph through the pocket water and plunge pools, with caddis, stoneflies and sculpin the forage, and a small olive sculpin along the undercut banks before the sun is on the water. NWS Charleston's 3:34 a.m. discussion has a cold front bringing showers and storms in this evening, widespread overnight and Thursday, with heavy downpours and training storms that could prompt localized flash flooding Thursday into Friday. The window is today.
waters.note: The Forest Service's Sept. 8 alert closes two sections of NFS Road 76, the Cranberry River Road, in the Gauley Ranger District through Nov. 20 for construction (Forest Order 09-21-02-26-05); that is the Cranberry, not the Williams. On FR 86 itself nothing has changed: the Aug. 12 alert still has the Tea Creek Campground bridge replacement under way since Aug. 28 with the bridge and campground open during the work, and the July 17 FR 86 closure alert has not been updated since it lapsed Aug. 31. No RLX watches, warnings or advisories were in effect for West Virginia at 3:34 a.m.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 24.9 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Flat at normal pool for a second day, and that is structure fishing: shad are the forage, so a white or pearl swimbait or a 3/4-ounce spoon over the wing-dam tips at first light, then a football jig or a Carolina-rigged craw dragged into the slack behind the tips once the sun is up. With no current to speak of, the bite is on the shade side of the riprap and the barge cuts through midday. The front due tonight puts rain on the Kanawha and Ohio tributaries Thursday and Friday, so the pool side above Byrd will colour and rise later in the week; this is the day before that.
waters.note: This is the pool side, 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam. USGS does not gauge the Byrd tailwater, and the Corps' Huntington District site (lrh.usace.army.mil) timed out on both tries this morning, so no lock or navigation notice is printed. NWS Charleston has no river watches or warnings in the district.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 26.4 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The Weather Service's forecast for the Huntington gauge, issued 10:10 a.m. Tuesday and read at 5 a.m., has the river at 26.0 feet by 8 a.m. today, 25.8 by early Thursday and 25.7 by Sunday, no flooding; the NWS observation at 5 a.m. was 26.45 feet, and the action stage at Huntington is 48 feet, so the river is 21 feet under it. Normal pool below Byrd means fishing structure, not current: shad and skipjack are the forage, so a skipjack-pattern swimbait or a white spinnerbait along the riprap and the lock wall early, and a crawfish-coloured jig pitched into the slack behind the barge cuts and the wing-dam tips when the sun gets on the water. Whatever current there is runs on the lock wall on lockage.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The Corps' Huntington District site could not be reached (two URLs, both timed out), so no lock notice is printed. The NWS forecast has not been reissued since Tuesday morning; a new one will follow the rain Thursday.

waters.reading: Sound highs 7:06 AM at 3.8 ft and 7:40 PM at 4.5 ft at Hampstead; lows 1:28 AM at 0.5 ft and 1:31 PM at 0.2 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 7:06 AM and 7:40 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The Fisherman's Post September report, published Tuesday, Sept. 1 and eight days old, has Jolly Roger Pier calling the Spanish and bluefish hit-or-miss for anglers sight-casting plugs, Surf City Pier's bottom fishing holding up with black drum, pompano and croakers, and inside, Native Son on a steady red drum bite at docks and creek mouths starting on topwater early and Carolina Flats on a strong class of 20-to-24-inch flounder with the mullet thick. Coastal Angler's Sept. 1 column, also eight days old, has slot reds on gold spoons and curly tails under a popping cork as the shrimp move. Reds want the last of the fall, which runs into the 1:31 PM low in the sound; flounder on the first of the flood at the creek mouths, then the push into the 7:40 PM high for trout on the grass edges. Waning crescent at 7%, two days from Thursday night's new moon, so the swings are building toward springs and the inlet current hardens. Water 79.7F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast.
waters.note: NWS Wilmington's 2:35 a.m. surf forecast has a moderate rip current risk for Pender beaches from 6 a.m. through this evening, 1-to-3-foot surf, east wind 5 to 10 mph, water around 80 and a very high UV index; Thursday moderate again with a southwest wind and a moderate waterspout risk. The overnight Coastal Flood Advisory (1:42 a.m.) is for inland New Hanover only, 9 to 11 p.m., on a 5.7-foot MLLW tide at Wilmington, 0.4 foot above normal; Pender is not in it. The National Hurricane Center's 2 a.m. Atlantic outlook expects no tropical cyclone formation in the next seven days and mentions nothing near Hispaniola or the Dominican Republic. New moon is 11:27 p.m. EDT Thursday, Sept. 10 (03:27 UTC Sept. 11), per the U.S. Naval Observatory. Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read.

kicker: The Aki basho opens Sunday in Tokyo, four days out; the NFL season opens tonight in Seattle at 8:20 p.m. ET, and Chelsea and Liverpool both kick off at 3 p.m.
